# Reset-free private-sign epochs: complete logical composition and real access costs

Status: candidate receiving/consequence note. The sign-pair theorem is received from PRIVATE_SIGN_PAIR_REDUCTION_CANDIDATE.md, SHA299bfbc80c35aed153b4c0ea2ebe1c8ea59dc4a0c289d4335b58f1669863f3c6, independently reviewed separately. This note does not claim randomness, twirling, adiabatic elimination or quadratic cancellation as new. It constructs a paid repeated protocol and identifies its calibration and conventional-comparator boundaries.

## 1. Received one-epoch contract

The known native source has an acquired pure-dark return certificate and source resolvent norm bound ell. The centered Hermitian interaction K has an acquired upper bound b, d>=||[H0,K]||, and the SAME source generator G and system H0 are used for both signs. Let

    C1=2d ell+16b^3 ell^2,
    C2=8bd ell^2+16b^4 ell^3.

The physical operation must implement sqrt(lambda)K and -sqrt(lambda)K while leaving G,H0 unchanged, or an actually equivalent conjugation protocol. A symbolic minus or a norm promise is not physical sign access.

For one duration t without internal user controls, choose a fresh private uniform sign and keep it fixed throughout that epoch. Discard the sign from the output. The accepted theorem bounds the complete reduced system/reference channel, UNIFORMLY for every joint source/system/reference initial state, by

    delta(t)<=A(t)/lambda+B(t)/lambda^(3/2),
    A(t)=A0+A1*t+C1^2*t^2,
    A0=12b^2 ell^2,
    A1=C2+6b ell C1,
    B(t)=C1*t*(8b^2 ell^2+C2*t).

The comparator is exp(t L_eff), with the same acquired effective CP jump stack. No source reset, stationary initial state, final source output or private-sign disclosure is in this contract.

## 2. Why fresh epochs compose without resetting memory

Partition the physical run into N epochs, placing a boundary at every prescribed system-only instrument. Choose each sign independently of the entire joint state and earlier records. The previous source and any private old signs may remain arbitrarily correlated with system/reference. Old private sign/controller registers must be idle or traced after their epoch and cease controlling later hardware; merely hiding a register that still changes later dynamics is not sufficient. They are NOT replaced by a fresh bath. Apply the one-epoch theorem to this actual joint input: its reduced output

# Independent review: reset-free sign epochs and actual access costs

Verdict: scoped mathematical/interface PASS. This receives the already reviewed sign-pair/epoch results and checks the additional gate, calibration and ordinary-comparator accounting; it is not another novelty or practical-advantage claim.

Source read in full: RESET_FREE_SIGN_EPOCHS_AND_ACCESS_COST.md, initially SHA3a2d595a89f219a960fa9ccce5f22a7b37cc8bdbcc0028843e5835ccf189f1d6. The two requested receiving clarifications were subsequently reread and the final SHA-256 verified as 11650859ab68db273f404b59954054e275e59010511d829d4a2bac7aa54e2c87. Date: 2026-10-31. Those changes explicitly require minimal-ceiling equal subdivision and old private controllers to cease controlling future hardware.

## Received schedule

Actual-state marginal induction is valid without bath reset under the previously reviewed uniform-input one-epoch contract. The final source now uses exactly ceil(Delta/tau) equal pieces per positive user-control interval, so its N bound is earned. It also explicitly makes old private registers idle or traced. These are needed conditions, not merely wording preferences.

The rational threshold, linear-time coefficients and zero-interaction convention agree with the earlier receipt. A dyadic cap in [tau/2,tau] doubles at most the 12b ell C1 endpoint-count contribution, while the existing linear and quadratic estimates cost at most 7b ell C1. Thus replacing 19 by 31 is safe. A tighter quadratic estimate could improve that number, but is unnecessary. Actual jitter must preserve the admitted maximum duration, total time and charged count; the statement does not erase finite-duration switching pulses.

## Exact involution and implementation errors

If an actual acquired system involution U anticommutes with K and commutes with H0, conjugating the positive joint channel by U at both ends gives exactly the negative-interaction channel with the same source generator. The supplied source is untouched. With user controls at boundaries, there are no hidden internal-control conjugations. Conservative cost is two U applications and one private fair bit per epoch; adjacent gates may be optimized only when their actual placement permits it.

For ||U_tilde−U||<=zeta, the unitary-channel error is at most 2zeta, so two boundary operations per epoch cost at most 4zeta and at most 4N zeta overall.
